title: Exclude test-only release content without scanner false positives
summary: Keep Tauri Rust test-only modules out of default portable packages while preserving explicit IncludeTests validation packages, and scan structured JSON values without misclassifying escaped test-inventory paths as live UNC values.
reason: Remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W09-010 and AUDIT-FIND-W10-020. Test modules live below the production Rust source tree and therefore bypass the release policy's existing top-level test exclusions, allowing developer-only literals and fixtures to ship by default. Raw-text scanning also mistook a valid JSON-escaped extended-path test anchor for a live UNC value and blocked canonical release packaging.
behavior_before: Default release builds omitted top-level test trees but copied apps/desktop/tauri/src-tauri/src/lib_tests and apps/desktop/tauri/src-tauri/src/backend_process/tests.rs because those test-only modules are nested under the production source tree. Content scanning also examined serialized JSON text and rejected the valid generated test inventory as if its escaped extended-path fixture were an operative UNC path.
behavior_after: Default release builds narrowly omit the Tauri lib_tests tree and backend_process/tests.rs, explicit IncludeTests builds retain them, and release hygiene verifies their absence whenever tests are not included. JSON content scanning traverses decoded string values, accepts the generated extended-path fixture, and continues rejecting actual private UNC values and malformed unsafe content.
tests_added: Release policy assertions prove all nested Tauri Rust test-module paths are excluded by default while production Rust source remains included.
Release policy and hygiene assertions prove explicit IncludeTests packages retain the nested Rust test modules.
A Rust-source privacy assertion forbids the audited personal server and user-profile identifiers.
Content-policy assertions parse JSON string values, distinguish escaped Windows extended drive-path fixtures from private UNC paths, and retain conservative scanning for malformed JSON.
manual_validation: PowerShell parser checks passed for the release policy, package test contracts, and release policy unit script.
Focused JSON content-policy checks passed against the generated test inventory and a synthetic private UNC value.
Release package policy checks passed, including a full default dry-run: 17,884 copied files planned, 10,883 excluded, and exactly four Tauri Rust test-module exclusions.

Actual default portable package built with 17,884 copied files; its manifest recorded four Tauri Rust test-module exclusions, all four test files were absent, adjacent production Rust was present, and packaged Rust had zero audited personal-identifier hits.

Actual package-mode manifest and hygiene checks passed. The broader testless self-test reached the known unrelated AUDIT-FIND-DEP-001 unallowlisted package-cycle baseline and therefore did not qualify as release acceptance.
Post-audit revalidation of Invoke-ReleasePackagePolicyChecks.ps1 passed, including the real generated test inventory, a 17,894-file current-tree dry-run, and the unsafe-content rejection path.
Project index/dependency graph and feature file map checks passed.
Release-scope, summary-integrity, feature-card, and risky-registry tooling passed: 37 tests and 70 subtests.
Risky-file registry and architecture guardrails passed; god-file guard reported the unchanged baseline of 0 errors and 51 warnings.
Global summary freshness reported only the same six pre-existing stale files outside this packet.
validate_changes --require-worktree-coverage passed with 1,149 valid packets before completion.
rollback_plan: Revert the narrow Rust test-module exclusions, hygiene rules, policy assertions, generated summaries/maps, and this packet together. Reassess release content scanning before permitting test-only source below production trees to ship by default.
notes: This batch changes release selection and package verification only. It does not launch the media pipeline or read, write, move, or delete media, so representative real-media validation is not required. The actual portable build used a uniquely named directory below the system temp root. Automated recursive cleanup was blocked by execution policy after validation, so the recoverable temp package remains at C:\Users\lmmye\AppData\Local\Temp\mediapipeline-w09-010-8a0eeb49efc9467da2556d07c1d9a791.
